questions.question: Why aren't a few hand-picked example questions enough to choose a retriever?
options: They take too long to run
They tend to favour the technique being shown, and a handful can't separate a real improvement from luck
They need a model call each
questions.explanation: A labelled set, metrics and a significance check replace impressions with evidence.

questions.question: What do graded relevance labels (2 = answers, 1 = related) let a metric reward?
options: Putting the answering document above merely related ones
questions.explanation: nDCG uses the grades; swapping a related doc above the answer lowers it.

questions.question: Why look at per-kind rows before the 'all' row?
options: The average hides where retrievers fail; here all the differences were in paraphrase queries
questions.explanation: If your users mostly paraphrase, the overall average overstates every system.

questions.question: Why was precision@3 low for every retriever?
options: Most queries have only one or two relevant documents, so even a perfect ranking can't fill three slots with relevant ones
questions.explanation: Compare precision between systems, not against 1.0.

questions.question: Hybrid beat BM25 by +0.042 nDCG with a 95% interval of [+0.000, +0.123]. What should you conclude?
options: This test set can't tell them apart yet; label more queries before claiming a win
questions.explanation: An interval that reaches 0 means the difference could be noise from 16 queries.

questions.question: What does 'paired' mean in the paired bootstrap?
options: Both systems are always scored on the same resampled queries, removing variation from some queries being harder
questions.explanation: Comparing on the same queries makes small, consistent differences detectable.
